topic: Prompt rules that say why: explain the reason behind an instruction and say what to do instead of what not to do (Anthropic prompting best practices)
text:
"NEVER use ellipses" is a weaker prompt than you'd think.

Anthropic's prompting guide gives two fixes for rules like that:

1. Say what to do. Not "Do not use markdown", but "Your response should be composed of smoothly flowing prose paragraphs."
2. Give the reason. Their example: "Your response will be read aloud by a text-to-speech engine, so never use ellipses since the text-to-speech engine will not know how to pronounce them."

The guide says Claude can generalize from the explanation. A bare rule covers one case. A reason can cover cases you didn't think of.

My rule of thumb: every "never" in a system prompt should get a "because" or a positive rewrite.

Which bare "never" in your prompts would you rewrite first?

image.alt: Before and after prompt: bare rule 'NEVER use ellipses' versus a rule that explains the text-to-speech reason, signed Ali Hassan, alihexan.com
